test.title: 50-question drill · every type, new numbers
test.intro: Fifty random questions covering Q1–Q7 (tables, validity, discrete, binomial, uniform, z, normal). Each stands alone: read it, solve on paper, type the answer, Check. Probabilities to 4 decimals; μ, σ to 2; x values to 1. z hints are printed like the real exam.

questions.prompt: Q1. Standard normal. Hint: area to the left of z = 0.57 is 0.7157.

parts.question: Find the area to the right of z = 0.57.

questions.prompt:
Q2. The number of overtime periods in a game (x) was recorded for 89 cases:
| x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| frequency | 8 | 25 | 28 | 28 |
First build the probability distribution: P(x) = frequency ÷ 89 (4 decimals): P(0) = 0.0899, P(1) = 0.2809, P(2) = 0.3146, P(3) = 0.3146.

parts.question: Find the probability that X is at most 2.

questions.prompt: Q3. Standard normal. Hints: area to the left of z = 1.96 is 0.9750; area to the left of z = −1.96 is 0.0250.

parts.question: Find the z-score that has area 0.0250 to its RIGHT.
parts.solution: RIGHT area given → convert: left area = 1 − 0.0250 = 0.9750 → the hint says z = 1.96

questions.prompt: Q4. Monthly cell-phone bills ($) are approximately normally distributed with mean μ = 72 and standard deviation σ = 11. Hint: the z-score with area 0.8 to its left is 0.84.

parts.question: What is the minimum value needed to be in the top 20%? Round to 1 decimal.

questions.prompt: Q5. The waiting time (minutes) for a bus is uniformly distributed between 5 and 25 minutes.

parts.question: Find the probability that the value is exactly 9 minutes.
parts.solution: A single value has no width under a continuous curve → P(X = one value) = 0

questions.prompt:
Q6. Coffee and shift. The table below summarizes 102 people.
| Shift | Day | Night | Total |
| Coffee | 20 | 7 | 27 |
| Tea | 26 | 16 | 42 |
| Neither | 7 | 26 | 33 |
| Total | 53 | 49 | 102 |

parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected person is "Neither" OR "Day"?
parts.solution:
OR → add both totals, subtract the overlap cell (Neither and Day = 7) once
P = 33/102 + 53/102 − 7/102 = 79/102 = 0.7745

questions.prompt:
Q7. The number of goals in a soccer match (x) was recorded for 123 cases:
| x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| frequency | 5 | 31 | 17 | 37 | 33 |
First build the probability distribution: P(x) = frequency ÷ 123 (4 decimals): P(0) = 0.0407, P(1) = 0.2520, P(2) = 0.1382, P(3) = 0.3008, P(4) = 0.2683.

parts.question: Find the probability that X is between 1 and 4, inclusive.

questions.prompt: Q8. According to a survey, 25% of students who commute by bus. A random sample of 8 is selected. Let X = the number in the sample who do.

parts.question: Find the probability that between 3 and 5 (inclusive) do.

questions.prompt:
Q9. Pet ownership and housing. The table below summarizes 132 people.
| Housing | Apartment | House | Total |
| Dog | 24 | 29 | 53 |
| Cat | 22 | 29 | 51 |
| No pet | 19 | 9 | 28 |
| Total | 65 | 67 | 132 |

parts.question: Two people are selected without replacement. What is the probability that at least one is "Apartment"?
parts.solution:
at least one → 1 − P(none) = 1 − P(both NOT Apartment)
P = 1 − 67/132 · 66/131 = 1 − 0.2557 = 0.7443

questions.prompt:
Q10. Major and class standing. The table below summarizes 117 people.

| Business | 18 | 27 | 45 |
| Science | 30 | 14 | 44 |
| Arts | 18 | 10 | 28 |
| Total | 66 | 51 | 117 |

parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected person is "Business" AND "Underclass"?
parts.solution:
AND → the one cell ÷ grand total
P = 18/117 = 0.1538

parts.question: What is the height of the probability density function (the rectangle)?

questions.prompt: Q13. The length (cm) of a machine-cut rod is uniformly distributed between 20 and 32 cm.

parts.question: Find the probability that the value is less than 23 cm.

questions.prompt: Q14. X is normal with μ = 80 and σ = 5. Hints: area to the left of z = −0.60 is 0.2743; area to the left of z = 2.40 is 0.9918.

parts.question: Find P(77 < X < 92).

questions.prompt:
Q16. Coffee and shift. The table below summarizes 114 people.
| Shift | Day | Night | Total |
| Coffee | 18 | 28 | 46 |
| Tea | 10 | 14 | 24 |
| Neither | 24 | 20 | 44 |
| Total | 52 | 62 | 114 |

parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected person is in the "Coffee" row?
parts.solution:
one category → its total ÷ grand total
P(Coffee) = 46/114 = 0.4035

questions.prompt: Q17. According to a survey, 35% of adults who own a smart speaker. A random sample of 8 is selected. Let X = the number in the sample who do.

parts.question: Find the probability that fewer than 3 do.

questions.prompt:
Q18. Consider the following table.
| x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| P(x) | 0.22 | 0.31 | 0.19 | ? | 0.08 |

parts.question: Find the value of P(3) that makes this a valid probability distribution.
parts.solution:
The probabilities must add to exactly 1
P(3) = 1 − (0.22 + 0.31 + 0.19 + 0.08) = 1 − 0.80 = 0.20

questions.prompt:
Q19. Pet ownership and housing. The table below summarizes 79 people.
| Housing | Apartment | House | Total |
| Dog | 6 | 13 | 19 |
| Cat | 10 | 20 | 30 |
| No pet | 19 | 11 | 30 |
| Total | 35 | 44 | 79 |

parts.question: Of the people in the "Dog" row, what proportion are "House"? (This is a GIVEN question.)
parts.solution:
"of the Dog people" = GIVEN Dog → divide by that row's total 19
P(House | Dog) = 13/19 = 0.6842

questions.prompt: Q20. According to a survey, 40% of customers who use a coupon. A random sample of 10 is selected. Let X = the number in the sample who do.

parts.question: Find the probability that at least 4 do.

questions.prompt: Q21. SAT math scores are approximately normally distributed with mean μ = 520 and standard deviation σ = 110. Hint: area to the left of z = 1.30 is 0.9032.

parts.question: Is a value of 663 unusual? (Unusual = tail probability below 0.05, or |z| > 2.)
Is this a valid discrete probability distribution?
parts.solution: Rule 1 ✓ · Rule 2: 0.10 + 0.25 + 0.30 + 0.25 + 0.15 = 1.05 ≠ 1 → NOT valid (the probabilities add to 1.05)

questions.prompt:
Q23. Consider the following table.
| x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| P(x) | 0.15 | 0.35 | 0.30 | 0.20 |

parts.question: Is this a valid discrete probability distribution?
parts.solution:
Rule 1: every P(x) is between 0 and 1 ✓
Rule 2: 0.15 + 0.35 + 0.30 + 0.20 = 1.00 ✓ → valid

parts.question: Find the expected number (mean) and the standard deviation of the number in the sample who do. (μ exact, σ to 2 decimals)

parts.question: The mean is μ = 2.29. Compute the standard deviation of X. Round to 2 decimals.

questions.prompt: Q28. Standard normal. Hints: area to the left of z = −1.41 is 0.0793; area to the left of z = 0.50 is 0.6915.

parts.question: Find the area between z = −1.41 and z = 0.50.
parts.solution: BETWEEN → (left of the bigger z) − (left of the smaller z) = 0.6915 − 0.0793 = 0.6122

First build the probability distribution: P(x) = frequency ÷ 152 (4 decimals): P(0) = 0.1645, P(1) = 0.2171, P(2) = 0.2368, P(3) = 0.1776, P(4) = 0.2039.

parts.question: Find the probability that X is more than 1.

questions.prompt: Q30. The amount of soda (oz) dispensed by a machine is uniformly distributed between 10 and 16 oz.

parts.question: Find the probability that the value is between 12 and 15 oz.

questions.prompt: Q31. Standard normal. Hints: area to the left of z = 1.96 is 0.9750; area to the left of z = 2.06 is 0.9803; area to the left of z = 1.86 is 0.9686.

parts.question: Find the z-score that has area 0.9750 to its LEFT.
parts.solution: backwards: the area is given → find the hint closest to 0.9750 → z = 1.96

questions.prompt: Q32. Systolic blood pressure of adults (mmHg) are approximately normally distributed with mean μ = 122 and standard deviation σ = 14. Hint: area to the left of z = −0.51 is 0.3050.

parts.question: Find the probability that a randomly selected value is below 114.8.
parts.solution:
z = (114.8 − 122)/14 = −0.51 → left area 0.3050
BELOW → the hint itself = 0.3050

questions.prompt: Q33. According to a survey, 10% of people who are left-handed. A random sample of 12 is selected. Let X = the number in the sample who do.

parts.question: Find the probability that none do.

questions.prompt:
Q34. Major and class standing. The table below summarizes 97 people.
| Standing | Underclass | Upperclass | Total |
| Business | 5 | 6 | 11 |
| Science | 19 | 8 | 27 |
| Arts | 30 | 29 | 59 |
| Total | 54 | 43 | 97 |

parts.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected person is NOT "Upperclass"?

questions.prompt: Q35. Battery life of a laptop (hours) are approximately normally distributed with mean μ = 9.2 and standard deviation σ = 1.4. Hint: the z-score with area 0.05 to its left is −1.645.

parts.question: What value separates the bottom 5% from the rest? Round to 1 decimal.
parts.solution:
bottom 5% → left area 0.05 → z = −1.645 (negative: below the mean)
x = μ + zσ = 9.2 + (−1.645)(1.4) = 6.9

questions.prompt:
Q36. Major and class standing. The table below summarizes 75 people.

| Business | 5 | 22 | 27 |
| Science | 7 | 14 | 21 |
| Arts | 10 | 17 | 27 |
| Total | 22 | 53 | 75 |

parts.question: Two people are selected without replacement. What is the probability that both are "Upperclass"?
parts.solution:
AND for two picks → multiply; the 2nd pick has one fewer Upperclass and one fewer person
P(both) = 53/75 · 52/74 = 0.4966

parts.question: Find the probability that the value is more than 87 seconds.

questions.prompt: Q38. Standard normal. Hint: area to the left of z = −1.96 is 0.0250.

parts.question: Find the area to the left of z = −1.96.
parts.solution: LEFT → the hint is the answer: P(Z < −1.96) = 0.0250

questions.prompt:
Q39. Consider the following table.
| x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| P(x) | 0.45 | 0.40 | 0.25 | −0.10 |

parts.question: Is this a valid discrete probability distribution?
parts.solution: Rule 1 fails: P(3) = −0.10 is below 0 → NOT valid (a probability can never be negative), even though the sum is 1

questions.prompt:
Q45. Pet ownership and housing. The table below summarizes 130 people.
| Housing | Apartment | House | Total |
| Dog | 20 | 12 | 32 |
| Cat | 20 | 27 | 47 |
| No pet | 25 | 26 | 51 |

parts.question: What is the probability that a person is "No pet" GIVEN that the person is "Apartment"?
parts.solution:
GIVEN → divide by the given group's total (Apartment = 65), not 130
P(No pet | Apartment) = 25/65 = 0.3846

questions.prompt: Q46. The weight (lb) of a bag of apples is uniformly distributed between 2 and 6 lb.

parts.question: 75% of the values are below what number? (Backwards: the area to the left is given.)
parts.solution: x = a + (area to the left)(b − a) = 2 + 0.75(4) = 2 + 3 = 5 lb

questions.prompt: Q47. Adult male heights (inches) are approximately normally distributed with mean μ = 69.5 and standard deviation σ = 2.8. Hint: area to the left of z = 1.25 is 0.8944.

questions.prompt: Q48. Weights of newborns (lb) are approximately normally distributed with mean μ = 7.5 and standard deviation σ = 1.1. Hint: the z-score for the 98th percentile is 2.05.

parts.question: Find the value at the 98th percentile. Round to 1 decimal.

questions.prompt: Q49. Standard normal. Hints: area to the left of z = −0.32 is 0.3745; area to the left of z = 0.76 is 0.7764.

parts.question: Find the area to the left of z = −0.32 OR to the right of z = 0.76 (the two tails).

questions.prompt: Q50. According to a survey, 30% of employees who work remotely. A random sample of 400 is selected. (μ = 120, σ = 9.17, and np(1 − p) = 84 ≥ 10.)

parts.question: Would it be unusual to find 118 in the sample who do?
parts.solution:
usual range = μ ± 2σ = 120 ± 2(9.17) = 101.66 to 138.34
118 is inside the range → not unusual
